employersPage.title: For employers
employersPage.lede: Post a role against the National Occupational Standards it actually requires, and see who can do the work — not who wrote the right words on a CV.

one.title: Hire against a standard, not a keyword
one.body: A role is described by the standards it needs, each with an importance and a mandatory flag. Two employers using the same standard mean the same thing, because the standard is national.

two.title: See who is nearly there
two.body: Ranking shows the candidates missing exactly one mandatory standard, and names it. That is a training decision rather than a rejection — and often the difference between filling a vacancy and reposting it.

three.title: Know what the market cannot supply
three.body: Every standard your roles ask for, counted against how many candidates hold it. A standard nobody holds is a hiring plan that will not work, and it is better to learn that before the vacancy is open.

employersPage.status: Employers now sign in and publish their own vacancies. Still to come: inviting colleagues, and verification so a candidate can tell a vetted employer from an unvetted one.

providersPage.title: For training organisations
providersPage.lede: Publish a course against the standards it teaches, and be recommended to the people whose specific gap it closes.

one.title: Recommended by gap, not by advertising
one.body: When a candidate is short of a role, courses are ranked by how much of that particular gap they close. A course teaching one thing they need beats a course teaching nine they already have.

two.title: Anchored to the national framework
two.body: Courses link to the same standards employers hire against, with the level each one teaches. That is what lets a course be matched to a vacancy rather than to a job title.

three.title: Entry routes come from the source
three.body: The qualification behind a role publishes its own ways in — education and experience alternatives, imported from the national corpus, not invented here.

providersPage.status: Providers now sign in and publish their own courses against the national framework. Still to come: inviting colleagues, and enrolment reporting.

aboutPage.title: About IISM
aboutPage.lede: A skills marketplace built on India's national qualification framework, so that what a person can do, what a job needs, and what a course teaches are all said in the same words.

one.title: One vocabulary
one.body: The National Occupational Standards are the shared language. A job's requirement, a candidate's claim and a course's syllabus all point at the same standard, which is what makes a gap computable at all.

two.title: Scores you can interrogate
two.body: Every match returns what was held, what is missing, which of those are mandatory, and the level shortfall. A model never decides a score here — it is deterministic, so it can be explained and measured.

three.title: Built for a low-end phone
three.body: Mobile-first, installable, in English and Hindi. The target device is an entry-level Android on mobile data, and that constraint shapes what gets built rather than being retrofitted.

aboutPage.status: Built in the open, sprint by sprint. The national taxonomy, matching, candidate profiles, employer sign-in and self-serve publishing for both vacancies and courses are live. Still to come: Hindi for the corpus itself — the interface is bilingual, the 21,303 standard names are not — along with verified organisations and semantic matching.

legal.draftNote: This text is written to be accurate about how IISM works today. It has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer and may change before public launch.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains what the Intelligent Integrated Skill Marketplace (IISM) holds about you, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

sections.title: Who is responsible
body: IISM is the data fiduciary for the personal data described here: we decide why and how it is processed. Questions and complaints go to our grievance officer — see the grievance page.

sections.title: What we hold
body: Your account: the mobile number or email address you sign up with, your name if you add one, your language, which version of this notice you agreed to and when, and when you withdrew consent if you did.

If you look for work: the profile you build — a headline, where you are (state and district), skills, experience, education, certifications, languages, the roles and places you prefer, and, if you choose to save it, the role you say you do now. You may also add your date of birth, your gender, the salary you expect, your notice period, the kind of work you want and whether you would relocate. Date of birth and gender are optional; gender is used only for equal-opportunity reporting. We also keep a numeric summary of your skills, which is how matching compares you with a vacancy.
If an agency programme signed you up on your behalf, a record of which programme did, and of the notice it attested was read to you.

Your applications and course interests, including any message you write, and what the employer or training provider replies. An employer may keep a private note about an application; it is included in the data you download.
Your batch interests: the batch, any message you write, and whether the training centre has contacted you, enrolled you or marked that you attended.
Updates and alerts we send you, and the offers an employer makes you. If you use the phone app, the code your phone gives us so an update can reach it.
Messages you send through the contact and grievance forms, and reports you make about a vacancy or course.
Activity: which matches, gaps and courses you open. These records are linked to your account and carry no name, number or email, and no list of your skills.
If you represent an organisation: its name, contact email and public profile, and the vacancies or courses it publishes.

We do not collect Aadhaar numbers or résumé files. A certification or assessment can add a mark to a skill (that you hold it, and how it was shown), never a score or a transcript. If this changes, this notice changes first.

sections.title: Why we hold it
body: To sign you in with a one-time code — there are no passwords.
To match job seekers with vacancies and courses against the National Occupational Standards, and to show each person the gap between them and a role.
To let employers see who could fill a vacancy. In an employer's candidate list you appear as a reference, headline, district, years of experience and skill gap — never your name, number or email.

When you apply for a vacancy, your name, phone number, email and any message you write are shared with that employer, for that vacancy. When you register interest in a course, they are shared with that training provider. When you register interest in a batch, they are shared with that training centre and with the owners and administrators of the organisation it belongs to, and with nobody else: not the organisation that sells the course, unless it is the same one. You are asked to confirm before any of these happens. Withdrawing the application or interest takes the details off their screen; they may already have used or noted them.
To tell you about vacancies that match your skills, by an in-app notice and email. You can turn these off in your profile.
To measure, in aggregate, whether the marketplace is working.

sections.title: Who else sees it
body: We do not sell personal data.

Service providers process it on our behalf and under contract: cloud hosting in India, and the SMS and email services that deliver sign-in codes. If you use the phone app, a push service delivers short notifications that carry fixed words and none of your details.

sections.title: How long we keep it
body: Your account and profile, your applications and course interests: until you delete your account.
Activity records and reports you made: 12 months, then deleted automatically.
Updates sent to you: 90 days once read or sent, 180 if never opened.
Messages you sent through the contact and grievance forms: one year after they are closed; open ones are kept until resolved.
The code your phone gave us for updates: until you sign out or delete your account.
Encrypted backups: replaced on a rolling schedule, so deleted data leaves them within that cycle.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Access: download everything we hold about you, as one file, from your Account page.
Correction: edit your profile at any time.

Withdrawing consent: from your Account page you can withdraw consent without deleting anything. Your account is paused: employers stop seeing you in their candidate lists, you receive no job alerts, nothing is tracked, no push notifications are sent, and you cannot apply or register interest. Applications and course interests that still show your details are withdrawn, and you are told how many before you confirm. You can still sign in, download your data, correct your profile and delete your account, and you come back by confirming this notice again. This is a pause, not an erasure.
Erasure: delete your account from your Account page. It is as easy as signing up, and it removes your profile and any organisation only you belong to.
Grievance: raise a complaint with our grievance officer; if it is not resolved, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India.
Nomination: you may nominate someone to exercise these rights for you in the event of death or incapacity — use the form on the grievance page.

sections.title: Children
body: The marketplace is for people aged 18 and over. When you sign up we ask you to confirm that you are, and we do not accept a date of birth that would make you younger. We do not knowingly create accounts for children.

sections.title: If something goes wrong
body: If personal data we hold is breached, we will tell the people affected and the Data Protection Board of India, as the law requires.

sections.title: Changes to this notice
body: Each version is dated. When the notice changes in a way that matters, we ask you to read it and confirm. Nothing is switched off while you decide.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of IISM. By creating an account you agree to them.

sections.title: The service
body: IISM connects job seekers, employers and training providers around the national skill standards. Matches and gaps are computed from those standards; they are guidance, not a guarantee of employment or admission.

sections.title: Your account
body: One person, one account. Keep your sign-in codes to yourself — anyone holding a code can sign in as you.
Give accurate information. Skills you add are shown as self-declared until evidence verifies them.

sections.title: Organisations
body: Publish only real vacancies and courses, with honest terms.
Never ask a job seeker to pay in return for a job or an interview.
Use what you see about candidates only to recruit for the vacancy it was shown against.

sections.title: What is not allowed
body: Scraping, bulk downloading or automated access beyond ordinary use.
Impersonating a person or organisation, or misrepresenting a qualification.
Trying to reach data that is not yours, or to disrupt the service.

sections.title: Suspension and closure
body: We may suspend an account that breaks these terms. You may close yours at any time from your Account page.

sections.title: Liability
body: IISM is provided as it is. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for decisions that employers, providers or job seekers make using it.

sections.title: Law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by the laws of India.

sections.title: Changes
body: Each version is dated. When the terms change in a way that matters, we ask you to agree again.

grievance.title: Grievance redressal
grievance.intro: If you have a complaint about how IISM handles your personal data, or about content on the marketplace, tell our grievance officer using the form on this page.

sections.title: How to raise a grievance
body: Use the form below. If you are signed in we answer through your account; if you are not, give an email address or mobile number we can reply to, so we can reach you.
Say what happened, when, and what you would like done. Do not send sign-in codes — we will never ask for them.

sections.title: What happens next
body: We acknowledge a grievance within 24 hours and aim to resolve it within 15 days.
If you are not satisfied with the outcome, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India.

sections.title: Things you can do yourself
body: Some requests need no one's help: download your data or delete your account from your Account page.

batchesUpload.title: Plan batches from a file
batchesUpload.intro: Check the file first. Nothing is made until you press the button at the end, and a batch you already planned is skipped, never changed. Batches are made as drafts: you publish them as a separate step.
batchesUpload.templateHelp: Each row is one batch: the course (its slug or exact title), the centre (its slug or exact name), the first and last day (year-month-day), the seats, and optionally the mode, a name, the days and times, and a fee. A course you are not authorised to deliver is a row with a problem.
batchesUpload.chooseFile: A CSV file, up to 2 MB
batchesUpload.tooBig: That file is larger than 2 MB. Split it and upload the parts one at a time.
batchesUpload.failed: Could not read that file. Check that it is a CSV and try again.
batchesUpload.summary: {ok} ready, {warnings} to look at, {errors} with a problem, {skipped} already planned.
batchesUpload.tableCaption: What each row of the file would do
batchesUpload.acknowledge: {count, plural, one {# row has a problem and will not be made.} other {# rows have a problem and will not be made.}} Make the others.
batchesUpload.apply: {count, plural, one {Make # draft batch} other {Make # draft batches}}
batchesUpload.created: {count, plural, one {# draft batch made.} other {# draft batches made.}}
batchesUpload.publishNote: Publishing makes a batch final: it can no longer be changed freely once learners register. A batch whose first day has passed, or whose course or arrangement is no longer in force, is refused and says why.
batchesUpload.publishConfirm: Publish {count, plural, one {# batch} other {# batches}}?
